title: Diadem mit Glaskameo
dimensions: 1,4 cm (Kameo); 33,5 cm (Goldband); 34,2 cm; Goldband max. 1,9 cm
description:
Art at the Imperial Court

Not only did the models for portrait types of the imperial family originate in the radius of the ruler, the court also set the style for fashion. In addition, the emperors advanced the arts right from the beginning and used them for their own representation. Cameos, raised relief images cut from precious stones, predominantly from layered agate, are especially connected with the ruling house as a special category of luxury. Presumably, they served as diplomatic gifts and representative pieces at court. Therefore, they advocated praise and self-image of the ruler, for instance via attributes of deities, more directly than was possible in publicly presented state art. Many of these cameos remained in the Imperial Treasury and returned to the West via Byzantium as princely gifts in the Middle Ages and then came into the possession of the Church by way of endowments.
Since the late 3rd century AD, the red porphyry from the imperial quarries in Egypt was exclusively reserved for the imperial dynasty due to its royal purple colour – for furnishings, building elements, sarcophagi or statues of rulers.

title: Römische Relieflagynos mit Liebespaaren
description:
Upper floor, room 6: "The Garden of Delights – The Art of Love in Antiquity"

Regarding their attitude towards sexuality, the Greeks, Etruscans and Romans fundamentally differed from today's Christian-occidental, Jewish or Muslim world. Eroticism and sexuality were present in all areas of ancient life. Be it at a banquet, at sports in the palaestra, on walls or in the gardens of Roman villas, in the Lupanar (brothel), in temples or even in the grave – everywhere there were pictures or allusions with sexual connotation, depictions of genitalia, symbols of fertility and lust. Even children were adorned with phallic amulets around their neck as talismans. Ancient literature dealt with the subject in all imaginable facets. The “ars amatoria” (Art of Love) by the Roman author Ovid is one of the most subtle poems on the subject ever written.
In the Archaeological National Museum of Naples, objects with erotic content from Pompeii and Herculaneum were collected in a room with limited access only for centuries, the “gabinetto segreto” (secret cabinet). In the 19th century, great demand for pertinent objects led to a large number of replicas and imitations, some of which were also acquired by the Berlin Museums. For a long time, classical studies avoided the subject; today it is a natural topic of research as regards various points of view, such as social history, perception of the body and gender roles.

Die Antikensammlung. Altes Museum, Pergamonmuseum 3. Aufl. (2007) S. 39 Nr. 15 (G. Platz).



A woman wearing a high head-dress, veil and earrings stands on a sphinx, the upper end culminating in a swan’s neck. This probably was part of a device, possibly a kithara (lyre), which was played during cultic rituals. The style is indicative of models from the Ancient Near East and from Egypt.

title: Goldener Zeremonialhut ("Berliner Goldhut")
description:
Bronzezeitlicher Zeremonialhut („Berliner Goldhut“), gefertigt aus einem Stück nahtlos getriebenem Goldblech und mit Kreisornamenten in Repousse-Technik verziert. Kalotte kegelförmig überhöht und mit breiter umlaufender Krempe. Krempe und Kalotte durch flaches Bronzeband verstärkt. An der Krempe außen tordierter Bronzedraht. 
Die Anordnung der Ornamentik auf Kalotte und Krempe des Zeremonialhutes wird als Darstellung eines Kalendersystems gedeutet, mit dem sich die Verschiebungen zwischen Sonnen- und Mondjahr berechnen und Mondfinsternisse voraussagen lassen.

title: Heroenrelief mit Darstellung der Dioskuren
description:
Die Bildfläche innerhalb einer glatten Umrahmung zeigt zwei einander zugewandte Reiter mit einem dünnen Baum zwischen ihnen, um dessen Zweige sich eine Schlange windet. Der linke Reiter hält der Schlange eine Opferschale (Phiale) hin. Dieses verbreitete Darstellungsschema repräsentiert fraglos die Dioskuren.

(Ausstellung "Pergamon - Panorama der antiken Metropole" 30.09.2011 - 30.09. 2012, Kat. Nr. 4.14)
